messages:
maya: Planning a targeted infra apply during the quiet window at 23:00 UTC tonight. Scope: tenant-fencing (IAM roles/policies) and cleanup of stale Route53 records. Need provider pin, canary plan, and a short rollback runbook.

deploybot: Apply window reserved: 2026-03-30 23:00 UTC. Preflight: plan-hash, state-lock, policy-check. Run link: https://deploy.internal/runs/0xab12

alex: Confirming targets: `-target=module.tenant_fence` then `-target=module.route53_cleanup`. Which provider version are we pinning?

maya: Pinning provider.aws to 4.28.0 and modules to commit hashes used in staging (sha: b3f2e1). We'll run canary against two tenants first.

sam: Reminder: last week a route change in staging caused latency for some edge nodes. Keep DNS TTL changes conservative (300->120).

maya: Good call. We'll keep TTL change minimal and validate resolver caches during canary.

deploybot: Merge freeze applied to `main` for the window: 1765550001 -> 1765553600. Overrides require `deploybot override --by ops-lead`.

ops-oncall: I'll be standing by. Setting short-term alerts: auth-error > 0.3% and DNS resolution failures > 1% will trigger rollback.

maya: Short checklist:
- export state snapshot to s3: s3://tf-state-backups/preapply-1765550001
- verify plan diff and output changes
- perform canary (tenants t-321,t-322) -> 10m validation
- if green: 50% -> 15m -> full
- rollback: reapply previous snapshot from s3 and reimport route53 recordsets if needed

alex: Plan excerpt (redacted):
```
+ aws_iam_role.tenant_api_role (module.tenant_fence)
~ aws_route53_record.service (module.route53_cleanup) ttl: 300 -> 120
```

sam: Canary command suggestion:
```bash
terraform apply -target=module.tenant_fence -var='tenants=["t-321","t-322"]'
```
Then validate logs and auth traces for 10m.

maya: Confirmed. Canary cadence set. Abort criteria: any auth 5xx spike >0.5% or sustained DNS failures >1% for 5m.

deploybot: Preflight results: plan-hash matches release notes, no provider upgrades queued, state lock available. Ready when ops-lead says GO.

taylor: Ops lead: GO for canary. I'll tag SRE for metric dashboards.

ops-oncall: Starting canary apply now. Watching auth latency, 5xx, and resolver metrics.

(monitoring) deploybot: Canary apply completed in 38s. No errors reported. run-id: 0xab12-canary

sam: Quick checks: resolver tests from us-east-1 and eu-west-1 passed, auth trace shows normal latencies.

ops-oncall: 10m canary window green. Proceeding to 50% rollout.

maya: Rolling to 50% tenants. Hold if any error rate increase >0.4% relative to baseline.

deploybot: 50% rollout finished. run-id: 0xab12-roll50

alex: Uploaded plan diff and apply logs to run: https://deploy.internal/runs/0xab12/logs (access controlled).

ops-oncall: 15m at 50% looks stable. No auth failures. Proceeding to full rollout.

maya: Full apply underway. Ops-oncall to escalate & trigger rollback on the thresholds we agreed.

deploybot: Full apply complete. final-plan-hash: 0xab12-final. No apply errors.

ops-oncall: Post-apply verification done: auth OK, DNS resolution OK, service pings within normal latency. Releasing merge freeze in 10m. Great coordination.

maya: Release notes snippet: provider.aws pinned to v4.28.0, modules pinned to sha b3f2e1, canary steps executed, rollback snapshot: s3://tf-state-backups/preapply-1765550001.

alex: Follow-up action: add automation to create s3 snapshot automatically before targeted applies and surface the snapshot link in deploy run metadata.

maya: Filed ticket for automation. Thanks everyone.
